newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada debt strategy to end 3-year bond issuance.
newsitem.headline: Canada debt strategy to end 3-year bond issuance.

text.p: The government of Canada said on Thursday that it intends to stop issuing three-year bonds as part of its 1997-98 debt strategy.

The Finance Ministry said in a statement that due to declining borrowing requirements Canada's 1997-98 bond program is planned to be up to 25 percent lower than last year and the government's treasury bill stock will fall about 10 percent.
"Due to the success of fiscal actions the government does not expect to borrow any new money from the market in 1998-99 and the debt-GDP ratio will soon be on a declining track," the statement said.
The ministry said it would ensure liquidity by continuing to build large benchmark bonds through quarterly issues at the two-, five-, 10- and 30-year maturities.

The government said that by the end of 1996-97 the net federal public debt is expected to have reached C$593.3 billion. Public debt charges in 1996-97 are estimated at C$45.5 billion, the first decline in three years, but still the largest single expenditure of the federal government.
The government said it will place emphasis on reducing its exposure to to interest rate changes by increasing the share of fixed rate debt to 65 percent in 1998.
The government said its 1997-98 borrowing requirement target is C$6.0 billion and will fall to C$1.0 billion in fiscal 1998-99.

The government said its long-term domestic debt management objective is to raise stable low-cost funding. Federal debt strategy in recent years has also pursued the objective of ensuring liquid and efficient domestic fixed-income markets.
